description.value: A multimodal neuroimaging study examining associations between gray matter volume measured with voxel-based morphometry and cerebral perfusion measured with arterial spin labeling in heroin-dependent patients under heroin and placebo conditions.

spans.text: Using a double-blind, within-subject design, heroin or placebo (saline) was administered to 14 heroin-dependent patients from a stable heroin-assisted treatment program, in order to observe acute short-term effects. Arterial spin labeling (ASL) was used to calculate perfusion quantification maps in both treatment conditions, while Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) was conducted to calculate regional GM density.

description.value: Double-blind, randomized crossover, within-subject study in which 14 heroin-dependent outpatients received intravenous heroin or placebo on separate scanning occasions approximately 8.4 days apart.

spans.text: In a cross-over, double-blind design, placebo (5 ml saline), and half of the daily heroin dose (mean = 176 ± 89.1 mg) were administered intravenously over a period of 30 s by a study nurse 20 min before the scanning session started.

description.value: ASL perfusion maps were calculated, converted to NIfTI, realigned, masked with binarized intracranial tissue, normalized to MNI space, smoothed, and proportionally scaled.

spans.text: Perfusion maps were first realigned and then masked with binarized intracranial tissue (binarization threshold: voxel intensity >0.1) to remove the extracerebral signal. Perfusion maps were then normalized to MNI space and smoothed using a 6 mm full-width-at half-maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel and proportionally scaled.
Cerebral blood flow (perfusion maps) was calculated by in-house software from ASL DICOM data.

value: perfusion quantification from label-control difference images

spans.text: The difference images of the label and control images were first calculated and the time course was fitted to an ideal flow model. The equation for perfusion was then solved ( 24 ).

description.value: MPRAGE images were processed with VBM in SPM8, including diffeomorphic normalization, tissue segmentation, modulation, and spatial smoothing.

spans.text: MPRAGE images were non-rigidly normalized to a population-based average using diffeomorphic anatomical registration through exponentiated lie algebra (DARTEL) ( 27 ). The segmented tissue maps of GM were modulated with the Jacobian determinants from the spatial normalization to correct for volume changes. Finally, images were smoothed with an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.
